title: Edge residency handshake and escrow test notes
content:
Purpose and scope

This is a working notes doc for designing and validating the operator-level handshake and escrow process used when a tenant is pinned to a region but their primary region becomes unavailable (capacity, legal freeze, outage). Focus areas: automated handshake between runtime + custody (escrow) bucket, operator evidence packaging, customer communication templates, and end-to-end test scenarios for both hard- and soft-pin flows at edge zones.

High-level goals
- Define deterministic escrow package contents for audit (what we store, how we sign it).
- Create reproducible handshake flows so routing, fallback, and eviction are observable and debuggable.
- Validate telemetry surfaces for billing/chargebacks during fallback/escrow periods.
- Give SRE and Legal a canonical test harness to prove compliance evidence for customer audits.

Open questions (top of mind)
1) Escrow TTL vs retention: what minimum evidence TTL does Legal want for a tenant pin swap? Suggestion: 90 days for initial pilot, escalate by contract. Need legal to confirm.
2) Signed evidence format: do we use JSON-LD + detached signature, or a binary signed archive? Ops prefers JSON-LD (readable), Legal may prefer signed tarball.
3) Failure modes where client keys cannot be rehydrated in fallback region (KMS jurisdiction): how to represent this in evidence without leaking secrets?
4) Customer opt-in: should escrow be default for enterprise or opt-in? Product input required.

Escrow package - proposed minimum schema (human-readable list here for tests)
- package_id (uuid)
- tenant_id
- original_region_pin (e.g., eu-west-1)
- fallback_region (if any)
- timestamp_of_handshake (ISO8601)
- operator_id (who initiated) or system-service id
- reason_code (capacity|legal_freeze|operator_action|customer_request)
- routing_snapshot (short list of service endpoints + versions)
- evidence_snapshot (hashes of payloads, sample headers, assertion logs)
- kms_key_manifest (public key IDs only, never private material)
- signed_manifest (detached signature of the manifest)
- retention_policy_label (90d|contract-365|audit-forever)

Note: For tests we will simulate two variants: (A) ephemeral-escrow (not full data move, just metadata & logs) and (B) full-escrow (move a day-of-traffic snapshot to escrow store).

Operator handshake flows (sketch)
1) Detection: region-health-monitor triggers condition (threshold) and writes candidate-handshake event to routing-controlplane.
2) Validation: automated pre-check job runs basic checks (tenant constraints, contract flags).
3) Create-escrow: create package/manifest, sign with system key, store to escrow-bucket with metadata.
4) Announce: update tenant routing state to fallback-policy, notify oncall and customer-notify-channel.
5) Execute-fallback: traffic begins routing to fallback region or degraded tier.
6) Post-check: telemetry verification (latency, token-cost delta, error rates).
7) Evidence-commit: after stabilization, mark escrow package as committed for retention and link to billing ledger.

End-to-end test matrix (operator-runner scenarios)
- Scenario A: soft-pin transient overload
  - Precondition: primary region at 85% CPU, ephemeral queue spike
  - Expected: automated soft-fallback (edge burst) within 45s, create-escrow (metadata-only), no contract escalation, telemetry tag: residency:soft-fallback
  - Verify: inbound requests served from fallback, manifest present in escrow-bucket, signed by system-key-01, retention label 90d

- Scenario B: hard-pin legal freeze (simulated)
  - Precondition: legal flag set for tenant (jurisdiction-block)
  - Expected: immediate hard-eviction from primary; full-escrow snapshot (24h) placed into customer-owned escrow vault, operator notification and legal ticket auto-created
  - Verify: evidence tarball checksum matches manifest, audit-signature present, KMS id references only (no private keys), billing changes recorded as 'legal-eviction'

- Scenario C: KMS unavailability in fallback region
  - Precondition: fallback region KMS returns 5xx for rewrap attempt
  - Expected: escrow manifest includes KMS failure code and mitigation steps attempted; routing should support degrade-to-hosted (if allowed) or pause requests; operator alert with runbook link
  - Verify: telemetry includes kms_rewrap_attempts, failure_reason, and operator ticket created

Observability and telemetry fields (must appear in test events)
- residency_event_id
- event_phase (detect|validate|create-escrow|announce|execute|post-check|commit)
- tenant_plan (self-serve|enterprise|sovereign)
- original_region, fallback_region
- escrow_package_id
- signed_by_key_id
- retention_label
- billing_marker (chargeback_code)
- latency_delta_ms
- token_cost_delta (estimated)
- evidence_size_bytes
- operator_id OR automated_system_id

Sample audit operator CLI snippets for tests
- create manifest (local dry-run):
  curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood.local/v1/escrow/dryrun -H "Authorization: Bearer ${OP_API_KEY}" -d '{"tenant_id":"t-1234","reason":"test-soft-fallback"}'

- commit escrow package:
  curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood.local/v1/escrow/commit -H "Authorization: Bearer ${OP_API_KEY}" -d '{"package_id":"pkg-uuid-1"}'

- retrieve manifest for evidence review:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${OP_API_KEY}" https://internal-api.redwood.local/v1/escrow/pkg-pkg-uuid-1/manifest

Customer communication templates (short drafts)
- Initial notice (automatic, short):
  Subject: Important: Temporary routing change for your workspace
  Body: We detected an infrastructure condition affecting {original_region}. To protect availability and compliance, your workspace traffic has been routed to {fallback_region}. No action required from you now; we will keep you updated and provide an evidence package if requested.

- Legal escalation (manual, detailed):
  Subject: Residency action summary & escrow evidence for {tenant_id}
  Body: Attached is the signed escrow package created on {timestamp}, including routing snapshot and evidence hashes. This package is retained under contract label {retention_label}. For questions, reply to compliance@redwood.com.

Runbook references for SRE
- runbook: residency-handshake-operator (internal)
- runbook: escrow-evidence-verification
- runbook: kms-rewrap-failures

Planned experiments (next 6 weeks)
1) Run 50 simulated soft-pin events across three tenants (self-serve vs enterprise) to measure median time-to-escrow and telemetry fidelity.
2) Validate signature format with Legal: trial both JSON-LD + detached sig and gzipped tar + detached sig. Capture feedback by week 2.
3) Integrate escrow retention labels with billing pipeline so the billing-team can test chargeback attribution for fallback periods.

Action items (owners)
- Marcus: prototype escrow manifest writer and storage API (due 2024-11-01).
- Aisha: schedule Legal sync re: signature format & retention (due 2024-10-25).
- Diego: implement telemetry tag patches for residency_event_id and event_phase (due 2024-11-08).
- Sofia: prepare operator test harness and CLI wrappers (due 2024-11-15).

Notes-to-self / loose ideas
- Consider using append-only object names (package_id + monotonic counter) in escrow-bucket to simplify evidence stitching for audits.
- Explore compact binary manifest for high-throughput events and readable JSON-LD for customer-facing packages.
- We should include minimal replay data (headers + 128KB sample per tenant) for quality investigation without full data transfer.

Links / refs
- Confluence: region-pin-spec (linked_artifacts above)
- Jira: JIRA-RESID-8721 (test harness epic)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/112 (routing-controlplane stash)


End of notes - trying to keep this document intentionally informal and actionable. Will convert to a polished runbook once legal and product confirm signatures and retention.
